A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations in Section 8 and Figures 1–2, comparing long-term performance and robustness in synthetic Markov games.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results in Section 8 and Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same robust Q-update, Nash-equilibrium oracle, value update and span-based stopping condition. The new weak-communication mapping is an existence-proof construction.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same structured random environment with 20 states, 5 actions and prosperous/deprived clusters. The new multichain counterexample is analytical, not an additional empirical scenario.

E2.justification: Section 8.1 retains discounted-reward Robust Nash-Iteration, citing Zhang et al. (2020) and Shi et al. (2024b). Section 8.2 retains non-robust average-reward Nash-Iteration, citing Li (2003).

E3.justification: The environment construction, KL uncertainty budget of 0.01, reported discount-factor range of 0.5–0.99, Player 1 reward metric and worst-case evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The discount-factor comparison and robustness comparison against a worst-case adversary are retained unchanged. No empirical ablation, sensitivity analysis or case study is added.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, or reports confidence intervals or significance tests. The figures retain the same curves without uncertainty bars.

E6.justification: All four plot panels in Figures 1–2 are identical across versions. The accompanying empirical findings and comparisons are also unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds a nonexistence argument in Lemma 3.1/Appendix B and weakly communicating existence results under Assumption 2 in Section 5/Appendix D. It removes v1 Appendix F's unichain argument, changes the NE definition from every initial state to an initial distribution, and adds uniqueness up to constants to Theorem 4.1 despite retaining contrary nonuniqueness prose.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion now claim stationary NE existence for weakly communicating games, extending the stated scope beyond v1's irreducible treatment and claimed unichain extension. The algorithmic and discounted-equilibrium contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes state-independent optimal gains from potentially state-dependent policy gains under weak communication and explains why a subset of best responses is used. Section 6 explicitly restricts algorithmic guarantees to irreducible games and identifies weakly communicating learning as open. These substantially refine applicability boundaries; the earlier PPAD-completeness caveat is removed.

D1.justification: The environment-generation details, uncertainty budget and policy-evaluation reference remain unchanged. No additional implementation settings, hardware, timing, or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang and Si (2025), supporting weak-communication and stationary-distribution literature, and discussion of general-sum learning algorithms. It expands the existing Bellman-proof critique and removes Deng et al. (2023) and Xu and Mannor (2010), while retaining the basic related-work framework.

P1.justification: The abstract and contributions are revised, and the Bellman/NE exposition and proof appendices are consolidated and reordered. Terminology and citation style change, and unfinished drafting prose disappears with v1 Appendix F. Much of the existing exposition remains.

P2.justification: The unchanged Figures 1–2 are grouped together on v2 page 10 instead of spanning v1 pages 9–10. Algorithm placement and surrounding layout shift, and running preprint headers are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix F's visibly unfinished proof and clarifies applicability boundaries. However, central new proofs have internal problems: Appendix B assigns player 2 the negative of player 1's worst-case payoff, inconsistent with separate worst-case minimization, and Lemma D.6 derives its unit bias bound by replacing M_n with m_n between (82) and (83). These undermine the new theoretical support, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
